purpose: Descriptive coverage pilot for #118 (post-Lasso partialling-out) and #119 (post-double-selection) on PR #129: 8 frozen Gaussian designs x 500 datasets, 5 arms on shared nuisance fits, 6 variance choices. Not a validation campaign; defaults unchanged.

cluster.note: Run on a Slurm cluster; resources were passed at submission.

recreation.cwd: benchmark/hdm/pilot (git worktree at the source commit, with ProximalBase.jl and ProximalSolvers.jl as sibling checkouts)
recreation.environment: Julia 1.13.3; pilot Project.toml path sources resolved before submission; JULIA_PKG_OFFLINE=true in jobs
commands: sbatch --parsable --job-name=RUNTAG --comment=RUNTAG --export=ALL,RUNTAG=...,TASKS=... run.sbatch (account, CPUs, memory and time passed at submission)
recreation.seeds: data Xoshiro(1_400_000_000 + 1_000_000 case + rep); solver Xoshiro(1_500_000_000 + 10_000_000 case + 10_000 rep + 10 slot + stream); disjoint from PR #86 blocks (max ~1.3002e9)

jobs.stage: canary (case 1 moderate, reps 1-2, 1 worker; also precompiles)
jobs.outcome: 100/100 arm records ok, 0 NaN se; 0.4865 s/rep (moderate, incl. convenience timings), warm-up 4.93 s; most elapsed time was precompilation

jobs.stage: main pilot (80 tasks = 8 cases x 10 chunks of 50 reps)
jobs.outcome: 80/80 tasks completed (80 worker steps COMPLETED); 180000/180000 arm records; zero exceptions

jobs.command: sbatch --parsable --job-name=hdm118-analysis-20261027 --comment=hdm118-analysis-20261027 --wrap='... srun --exact -n1 -c2 julia --project=. analyze.jl outputs/hdm118-pilot-20261027 results/20261027'

outputs.raw_records: Not retained. The per-task record CSVs were deleted after analysis; summary.csv holds every reported quantity.

validation.checks: sacct exit codes for all steps; record count 180000/180000 and zero exception rows (analysis); canary record sanity (100/100 ok, no NaN se); downloaded archive sha256 equals the cluster copy
validation.not_performed: No independent refit of individual records; the statistical code paths were verified by unit tests and R golden comparisons in U1-U5.
